findings.title: exemptions.schema.json reason minLength raised 24→40 turns a graceful per-entry FAIL into a whole-ledger crash
findings.before: "reason": {"type": "string", "minLength": 24, "description": "≥ 40 chars on scope finding — CFG.EXEMPTIONS checks the longer bound"}
findings.after: "reason": {"type": "string", "minLength": 40, "description": "at least 40 characters, as CFG.EXEMPTIONS enforces for every entry: what is declined and why"}
findings.why_it_matters: Doctor.jl's CFG.EXEMPTIONS already enforced `length(e["reason"]) >= 40` for every entry unconditionally at base (unchanged by this diff), so a compliant ledger is unaffected. But an already-noncompliant ledger (a reason of 24-39 characters, which used to schema-validate fine and merely make `gbg doctor` FAIL CFG.EXEMPTIONS while every other command kept working with the rest of the ledger honoured) now makes `Ledger.read` throw a `LedgerError` at schema-validation time instead. That exception empties `ctx.ledger` entirely in Doctor.jl (caught, reported as one FAIL — no regression there), but `Scan.jl`'s `scan_docs`/`scan_html` call `Ledger.read(cfg)` with no surrounding try/catch, so the same ledger that used to let `gbg scan docs` run to completion (with every OTHER exemption in the file still honoured) now crashes that command outright, and blinds every unrelated exemption in the same file, not just the offending entry.
findings.description: The fix narrows a genuine schema/code inconsistency (schema said 24, the doctor's own code required 40) but does so by moving the enforcement point earlier, from an itemized, gracefully-reported doctor FAIL naming just the bad entry, into an unguarded exception that (a) empties the whole ledger rather than rejecting only the one entry and (b) is only caught at one of several call sites (Doctor.jl), not at Scan.jl's `scan_docs`/`scan_html`, which read the ledger directly and uncaught. The defect being fixed (a stale schema description) did not require widening the failure's blast radius or its exit-code path.
findings.evidence: Doctor.jl (unchanged by this diff): `length(e["reason"]) >= 40 || push!(errs, "$tag: reason shorter than 40 characters")`. Scan.jl:423 (unchanged): `ledger = Ledger.read(cfg)` with no try/catch around it, inside `scan_docs`. Ledger.jl:35-36 (unchanged): `errs = validate(...); isempty(errs) || throw(LedgerError(...))`.

findings.title: signature_fidelity's `examined` counter now silently excludes extension-homed bindings, with no test locking in either value
findings.before:
examined === nothing || (examined[] += 1)                 # what was COMPARED: the scan's population
if def === :extension
    push!(out, "$name: EXTENSION-HOMED (no methods loaded) — skipped"); continue
end
findings.after:
if def === :extension
    push!(out, "$name: EXTENSION-HOMED (no methods loaded) — skipped"); continue
end
examined === nothing || (examined[] += 1)                 # what was COMPARED: the scan's population
findings.why_it_matters: For any consumer package with public bindings homed in an extension module (no methods loaded when `signature_fidelity` runs), the reported `examined` population now excludes them, whereas before they inflated the count despite zero comparisons happening for them. `src/Scans/signature_fidelity.jl` uses this exact count as the scan's reported population, which feeds the DEAD/clean distinction the scan's own header comment cites ("the population is the number of bindings COMPARED... this printed clean over 74 files while examining zero"). The change is defensible as a correctness fix — the count now genuinely reflects work done — but it silently changes a previously-computed, user-visible number (a population count in scan output) for previously valid input, and no test in the diff exercises either the old or the new value.
findings.description: The reordering makes `examined` consistent with the long-standing docstring sentence 'an extension-homed binding with no methods loaded is reported as skipped' (present, unchanged in wording, at both base and head) — skipped bindings were nonetheless being counted as 'examined/compared' before this diff, which is the same class of bug the scan's own comment warns about, just in an extension-homed rather than zero-export package. The fix is narrowly scoped to the one branch it corrects.
findings.evidence: src/Reflection.jl diff hunk moving `examined === nothing || (examined[] += 1)` from before to after the `if def === :extension ... continue end` block; src/Scans/signature_fidelity.jl (unchanged): `return (hits, examined[])`.
